subject: BluePeak MAP: performance targets & streaming TTFT evaluation
body:
From: Samuel Kim <samuel.kim@bluepeakhealth.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement <procurement@bluepeakhealth.com>
Date: Tue, 7 Nov 2028 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: MAP & perf targets for streaming chat - BluePeak/Redwood

Hi Vanessa,

Thanks again for yesterday's demo. BluePeak's platform team needs a short Mutual Action Plan that includes the performance targets and an evaluation plan we can hand to infra. We also need provisional numbers for TTFT for streaming chat so procurement can kick off the SOW review.

High level asks:
- Target TTFT (p50/p95/p99) for our baseline conversation profile (average prompt length ~45 tokens, average completion ~120 tokens)
- Expected throughput at concurrency levels 50, 200, 500 agents
- Streaming latency behavior (first-byte, token-emit latency distribution)
- Test harness and artifacts you will share so we can reproduce results

Can you get a MAP + an initial bench report over the next 48 hours? Procurement is copied for timing.

Thanks,
Samuel
Head of ML Infrastructure
BluePeak Health

----

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.ai>
To: Samuel Kim <samuel.kim@bluepeakhealth.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 7 Nov 2028 11:05:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: MAP & perf targets for streaming chat - BluePeak/Redwood

Samuel — attaching a draft MAP and a short PDF with our TTFT p50/p95/p99 definitions and measurement methodology. See attachments: BP_MAP_v3.xlsx, redwood-ttft-p95-p99.pdf.

Executive summary / proposed MAP milestones:
- Day 0 (today): Agreement on workloads and acceptance criteria (this thread)
- Day 1-2: Redwood runs two benchmark sweeps (baseline & stress) and shares results + raw CSVs
- Day 3: Joint review call to go over findings and any model choice trade-offs
- Day 4-10: Canary plan & A/B rollout (optional) with acceptance gating at p95 TTFT and streaming token-drop checks
- Week 3-6: Production roll + final SOW signing and capacity reservation

Evaluation plan (short):
- Models: redwood-13b-quant (primary), redwood-7b-quant (fallback)
- Workloads: 3 buckets (low, typical, peak) derived from your sample traces
- Measurements:
  - TTFT (time-to-first-token) measured as server-side emit timestamp minus request-receipt; report p50/p95/p99
  - Streaming token latency distribution (per-token emit jitter) over session length
  - Throughput: RPS sustained at target concurrency with 99% token delivery success (no stream truncation)
  - Cost: per-token estimate at the observed throughput and batching settings
- Harness: harness repo + k6 scripts + raw trace CSVs will be shared.

Proposed acceptance targets (initial):
- Typical workload (concurrency 200): TTFT p50 <= 180ms, p95 <= 420ms, p99 <= 950ms
- Peak (concurrency 500): TTFT p50 <= 240ms, p95 <= 650ms, p99 <= 1.6s
- Streaming per-token p95 latency <= 60ms for mid-length tokens

Next steps: if those targets look reasonable, we will run the two sweeps and post results in this thread. If you want tighter p99s we can discuss quantization and reserved capacity options.

Thanks — forwarding attachments now.
Vanessa Ortiz
Director, Solutions
Redwood Inference

----

From: Samuel Kim <samuel.kim@bluepeakhealth.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement <procurement@bluepeakhealth.com>
Date: Tue, 7 Nov 2028 13:47:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: MAP & perf targets for streaming chat - BluePeak/Redwood

Vanessa — appreciate the quick proposal. A few clarifying Qs before you run the sweeps:
1) For the typical workload, does concurrency=200 assume sticky session routing (per-user KV cache) or cold starts?
2) Will TTFT numbers include network latency to our VPC (we expect ~10-20ms additional RTT)?
3) For p99 targets, we may prefer a guarded SLA (reserved capacity) during our canary window — please flag what changes if we move to Dedicated.

Procurement: what's the earliest we can have the SOW draft for review?

Best,
Samuel

----

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.ai>
To: Samuel Kim <samuel.kim@bluepeakhealth.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.ai>, procurement <procurement@bluepeakhealth.com>
Date: Wed, 8 Nov 2028 08:22:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: MAP & perf targets for streaming chat - BluePeak/Redwood

Samuel — quick answers and results from our first sweep (attached as bp-bench-results-20281107.csv):
- Concurrency note: our typical-concurrency=200 run used sticky routing and warm KV cache; we included a cold-start sweep in the stress run (csv includes both).
- Network: the reported TTFTs are server-side emit times; please add estimated egress/RPC RTT (we logged ~12ms to us-west-2 simulated VPC).
- Dedicated: moving to Dedicated (reserved pool) tightens p99 by ~20-30% depending on queuing — we'll outline delta in the final MAP.

Preliminary numbers (redwood-13b-quant, streaming enabled, batching tuned for latency):
- Typical (concurrency 200): TTFT p50 = 165ms, p95 = 390ms, p99 = 880ms
- Peak (concurrency 500): TTFT p50 = 235ms, p95 = 610ms, p99 = 1.48s
- Throughput: sustained 1,200 RPS with token delivery success 99.9% at concurrency 200 when using batch_size=8 and continuous batching window 12ms
- Streaming per-token latency: p50=18ms, p95=54ms, p99=120ms (observed jitter spikes correlate with long completions >400 tokens)

Requested artifacts attached. If these look OK we can schedule the joint review call today or tomorrow.

Attachments: bp-bench-results-20281107.csv (csv, 1.1MB), BP_MAP_v3.xlsx (xlsx, 420KB)

Thanks,
Vanessa

I'll sync legal on the draft SOW after you confirm the bench CSV looks clean.

-Marcus
